title: All I Want for Christmas Is You
hook: The up-tempo "I just want you for my own" period: two statements of the rising-and-falling opening line, the leap to the high "make my wish come true", and the title line closing on the long held G

evidence.summary: Primary: Hooktheory public JSON "Pre-Chorus and Chorus" (SHA-256 f4ef90bf...), G major, 150 BPM, notes 0-33 frozen as a derived MIDI at PPQ 9600 with documented edits: Hooktheory-only sixteenths E4 D4 (notes 25-26) dropped, the "all I want for Christmas" run (notes 23-29) re-timed to the recording, three holds lengthened to the recording. Reference: the lead vocal of the original recording (official lyric video NrGGIoDL6U4, 4:01 album version), Demucs htdemucs vocal stem, pyin segments plus CQT: 31 of 32 pitches equal in order at shift 0 (the second-line A4, position 9, is only a sliding stub); onsets within 0.5 beat except the retimed run. No second symbolic transcription was available (MIDI Show files need a login), so the independent evidence is the recording itself. The phrase shares its melody with the verse in the slow intro and the repeat at 104 s; the verse, which starts on G3, cannot be joined to it (span 19).

corpus.notes: Pitch audit against the original recording (vocal stem pyin + CQT); matching clip kept outside the corpus at out/catalogue-2026-11-22/mariah/sources/original-clip-82.0-99.5s.flac: 82.0-99.5 s of the official lyric video audio; the first sung note starts 1.43 s into the clip. Alignment kept unvalidated; not indexed in the corpus.

title: Jingle Bells
hook: One complete stanza as sung today: the verse "Dashing through the snow ... a sleighing song tonight" followed by the whole chorus, "Jingle bells, jingle bells ... one-horse open sleigh" twice, the second time resolving to the tonic

evidence.summary: Primary: CPDL 66808 (William Hale, "adapts Pierpont's own arrangement as given in the original edition [Boston: Oliver Ditson, 1857] to the tune in the standard modern form", Allegro 2/4, A-flat major, 130 BPM): engraved PDF read page by page, verse = the voice staff (bars 9-24), chorus = the soprano of the S/A staff (bars 25-40), events selected by position (voice 0-46 minus the parenthesised Eb4 pickup 22; S/A soprano rows listed in recipe.cjs), frozen as a derived MIDI at PPQ 9600 with documented edits (snow and way held, "fun it" dotted twice, final sleigh held 2 beats; jingle-bells-edits.json). Pitch sequence of all 96 notes equal to: Hooktheory "Verse" and "Chorus" (James Lord Pierpont page, A major, separately authored; shift -1; its 4th E5 of "ride and sing a" is merged and it adds three lead-in notes: E4 pickup, and E5 after "tonight" and after the chorus first half), and the Calgary ABC file (C major; all 96 pitches equal at +4, its g2 lead-ins excluded). Rhythm checked against all three: attacks equal except the edited places. The 1857 first-edition chorus (CPDL 66801) is a different melody (C C C, E-flat E-flat E-flat, C C F F E); this phrase is the standard modern chorus on the repeated E E E.

corpus.notes: Public-domain tune with no single canonical recording: no original clip kept and no recording audit; the evidence is the 1857-derived score plus two independent transcriptions.

title: Last Christmas
hook: The complete chorus in both halves: the two-note call and its answer, the rising turn up to the held D, then the second half that climbs to the high G before easing down to the final held A

evidence.summary: Primary: Hooktheory public JSON "Chorus" (SHA-256 f9579a7b...), D major, 34 notes over 8 bars, frozen as a derived MIDI at PPQ 9600 at 107 BPM (the tab says 108; the recording measures 0.561 and 0.563 s per beat) with four documented timing edits read from the recording: the first note and two late entries retimed, and the final held A3 lengthened from 2 to 3 beats. Reference: the lead vocal of the original recording (official video E8gmARGvPlI, 1984 single), Demucs htdemucs vocal stem, pyin segments plus RMS and CQT: the chorus is sung twice back to back (18.3 s and 36.2 s) and both passes match all 34 pitches in order at shift 0 (recording 0.45 semitone flat; the repeated-E4 pairs are split at RMS dips; A3 at position 3 is sung about a semitone flat and slid in the first pass, a clean A3 in the second; the short B3 at position 21 is audible only in the CQT); onsets within 0.25 beat apart from the first note. No second symbolic transcription of the vocal was available; the independent evidence is the recording itself.

corpus.notes: Pitch audit against the original recording (vocal stem pyin + RMS + CQT, both chorus passes); matching clip kept outside the corpus at out/catalogue-2026-11-22/last-christmas/sources/original-clip-17.5-36.1s.flac: 17.5-36.1 s of the official video audio; the first sung note starts 0.67 s into the clip. Alignment kept unvalidated; not indexed in the corpus.

title: Feliz Navidad
hook: One complete statement as sung: the Spanish section (the three-fold two-bar greeting and its closing wish) followed by the English section (the climbing wish, the lower answer, the climbing wish again and the closing line down to the held final D)

evidence.summary: Primary: Hooktheory public JSON "Chorus" (SHA-256 6a5438f2...), D major, 66 notes over 16 bars (Spanish section 25 notes, English section 41 notes), frozen as a derived MIDI at PPQ 9600 at 148 BPM with one documented edit read from the recording (the second C# of the closing line held through the one-beat rest, 0.5 to 1.5 beats). Reference: the lead vocal of the original 1970 recording (official audio N8NcQzMQN_U), Demucs htdemucs vocal stem, pyin segments plus RMS: the recording sings the Spanish section twice (13.1 s and 26.1 s) and then the English section twice (38.7 s and 51.6 s). The second Spanish pass followed directly by the first English pass match all 66 pitches in order at shift 0 (no tuning offset: median sung pitch +0.1 semitone from the tab, all notes within -0.4 to +0.6): 55 are read from separate vocal segments and 11 sit inside repeated-pitch runs that pyin merges, whose attacks were checked against RMS dips (3.0 dB or more at 19 of the 21 repeated pairs in both passes; the legato second syllables at positions 17 and 37 dip only 1.7 to 3.8 dB). The other two passes (13.1 s and 51.6 s) were audited the same way with matching contours. Onsets agree within 0.6 beat; the recording is ornamented (scoops, grace notes, ad libs) and those are not part of the melody. No second symbolic transcription of the vocal was available; the independent evidence is the recording itself.

corpus.notes: Pitch audit against the original recording (vocal stem pyin + RMS, four passes); matching clip kept outside the corpus at out/catalogue-2026-11-22/feliz-navidad/sources/original-clip-25.8-51.8s.flac: 25.8-51.8 s of the official audio (second Spanish pass and first English pass); the first sung note starts 0.33 s into the clip. Alignment kept unvalidated; not indexed in the corpus.

title: Jingle Bell Rock
hook: The complete 16-bar first verse as sung, in two eight-bar halves: the repeated-note title hook and its low answer, the answering line, the climbing third line and the closing line, then the same first three lines with their own closing line that settles on the held final D

evidence.summary: Primary: Hooktheory public JSON "Verse" (SHA-256 e55fac3a...), D major, 37 notes over 8 bars, frozen as a derived MIDI at PPQ 9600 at 121 BPM for the first half; the second half repeats its first three lines (all 29 notes, checked against the recording) and ends with a 4-note closing line read from the recording because the Hooktheory "Chorus"/"Outro" tabs of the same section do not match the recording there (they merge the held B3 of the second line and write a different closing line). Two documented edits to the first line (the B3 before the low F#3 shortened to half a beat, the low F#3 moved to beat 5.5 and held one beat) plus a 2/3 shuffle on every off-beat eighth (recording: off-beat onsets +0.16 and +0.17 beat late in the two halves, on-beat 0.00; tab swing 0.64-0.66). Reference: the lead vocal of the original recording (YouTube Topic upload uAolgbXsge0, 2:10, the 1957 single), Demucs htdemucs vocal stem, pyin segments plus RMS dips and spectrograms: both halves back to back (first half 7.9 s, second half 23.8 s), 64 of 70 pitches match in order at shift 0 (median recording offset -0.10 semitone, no offset applied; repeated pitches split at RMS dips; six notes of the first half are not readable in the stem and are absent; every one of them is read in the second half); onsets within 0.3 beat of the shuffled grid (build check 0.29, median 0.00; the largest are the slid-into A3 of the third line and the last two notes of the second half). No second symbolic transcription of the full 16 bars was available; the independent evidence is the recording itself.

corpus.notes: Pitch audit against the original recording (vocal stem pyin + RMS dips + spectrograms, both halves); matching clip kept outside the corpus at out/catalogue-2026-11-22/jingle-bell-rock/sources/original-clip-7.3-39.0s.flac: 7.3-39.0 s of the Topic upload audio; the first sung note starts about 0.6 s into the clip. Alignment kept unvalidated; not indexed in the corpus.

title: Carol of the Bells
hook: The complete first period of the melody voice in the standard Wilhousky arrangement (bars 17-24 of the SATB score): four statements of the four-note ostinato, the descending line and its cadence

evidence.summary: Primary: the engraved SATB score of Leontovych / Wilhousky (G minor, 3/4, 69 bars) shown by the free notation video "Carol of the bells (arr. Peter J. Wilhousky)" (Listen & Read, choir of the Church of St. Andrew & St. Paul, Montreal): soprano staff, bars 17-24, read by eye from frames at 22 s, 29 s and 34 s (SHA-256 of the frames and of 2x crops stored beside the recipe), transcribed by hand into a derived MIDI at PPQ 9600, 150 BPM (tempo is editorial). Boundaries: the soprano sings the lower ostinato Bb4 A4 Bb4 G4 in bars 1-16, the upper ostinato D5 C5 D5 Bb4 in bars 17-20, the descending line G5 .. D5 .. C5 in bars 21-23 and the G4 cadence in bar 24; bar 25 starts the rising Merry scale, a new section. Rhythm: quarter, two eighths, quarter per ostinato bar; quarter, two eighths and a slurred eighth pair in bars 21-23; written values kept (staccato dots not shortened). Compared event by event (35 pitches, onsets, durations): Hooktheory John Williams "Carol Of The Bells" Chorus (G-sharp minor, separately authored, shift -1) all equal; Hooktheory Trans-Siberian Orchestra (E minor, indices 16-50, shift +3) all equal. Both are Hooktheory user transcriptions of choral-derived arrangements; source-family independence from the score is not proven. The tune is the public-domain Shchedryk melody (Leontovych, 1914).

corpus.notes: Public-domain tune with no single canonical recording: no original clip kept and no recording audit; the evidence is the engraved Wilhousky score plus two independent Hooktheory transcriptions.

title: Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer
hook: The complete 16-bar main verse as Gene Autry sings it, in two eight-bar halves: the rocking opening line with its upward leap and long held note, the answering line that rises to a held top note, the descending third line and the closing line of alternating repeated notes, then the same three lines again with a new closing line that leaps to the top and settles on the long held tonic

evidence.summary: Primary: the free lead sheet "Rudolph the Red Nosed Reindeer" arranged by Mikael Baggstrom on professionalcomposers.com (PNG SHA-256 0674cac1...), C major, 4/4; bars 2-17 (A + A-prime, 56 notes, ending on the held tonic C) transcribed by hand and written as a derived MIDI at PPQ 9600, 143.2 BPM, with a 2/3 shuffle on every off-beat eighth (the recording is swung: median onset deviation from the swung grid 0.01 beat) and the line-final held Gs of lines 1 and 3 of each half ended a third of a beat early so the next line's repeated G is heard (the karaoke MIDIs end them at 2.2-2.75 of 3 beats; the recording ends them much earlier, see NOTES). Corroboration 1: four community karaoke MIDIs from BitMidi (uploads 90184, 90187, 90188, 90189; ancestry unknown), all 56 notes including the final bar: every pitch interval equals the lead sheet in every file; onsets agree on the swung grid (90184 exactly, 90188 within 0.03 beat) or the straight grid (90187, 90189, within 0.03 beat); they shorten several lengths against the lead sheet, which the recording also does. Corroboration 2: the lead vocal of the Gene Autry recording (official channel audio 44bL90HP0Ys, edition not stated, Demucs htdemucs vocal stem, pyin, RMS): A at 23.8-36.0 s and A-prime at 37.2-49.9 s, all 56 notes read in order, including the closing bar (the leap to the top note, a scoop reaching A3 at its end, then the held tonic). Fit: the singer slows down (A 145.5 BPM, A-prime 142.5, whole 143.2); onsets within 0.43 beat of the swung grid of each half except note 26 (0.67 beat early); recording about 0.65 semitone sharp (no offset applied); raw pitch within 1.6 semitones of the lead sheet for every note (within 1.0 after removing the offset) except three slid notes: the second note of line 3 (sung 1.55 semitones low in A and 1.85 low in A-prime after the offset) and the C5 leap of line 2 in A (a scoop, 1.7 low overall, right pitch only at its end). No Hooktheory page exists for this song (artist pages of Gene Autry and other candidates checked). The recording is a swing band with slides: the vocal stem is a pitch and onset audit, not a note-for-note transcription.

corpus.notes: Pitch and onset audit against the original recording (vocal stem pyin + RMS, A at 23.8-36.0 s, A-prime at 37.2-49.9 s); matching clip kept outside the corpus at out/catalogue-2026-11-22/rudolph/sources/original-clip-23.3-50.4s.flac (the first sung note starts about 0.5 s into the clip). Alignment kept unvalidated; not indexed in the corpus.
